### 1. Checkout & Build
- Use GitHub Actions `actions/checkout@v3`.

### 2. Build & Push Docker Image

- Note: This stage blocks promotion to production if load test fails.

### 4. Canary Deployment Rollout
- Deploy new version to EKS fin-prod-01 using a canary deployment strategy.
- Initial traffic split: 5.00% routed to new version, 95.00% to stable version.
- Use Kubernetes deployment tooling (e.g., Argo Rollouts, Flagger) or custom scripts to control rollout.

- Rollback mechanism should automatically revert to the previous stable version upon trigger.
- Implement health checks and readiness probes to avoid traffic to unhealthy pods.

### 6. Promotion to Full Production
- Upon successful canary period with no rollback trigger:
  - Shift 100% traffic to new version.
  - Confirm stability via Datadog monitoring.

### 7. Deployment Notification
- Notify Slack channel `#deployments` at key points:
  - Deployment started

      - name: Update kubeconfig for EKS cluster

          # Apply the canary deployment manifest (assumed to be templated to use image tag and traffic split)

          kubectl -n default patch canary financial-reporting-canary -p "{\"spec\":{\"trafficRouting\":{\"weights\":{\"canary\":5,\"stable\":95}}}}"

      - name: Monitor Deployment with Datadog and Rollback on Error Rate > 2%
        id: monitor
        run: |
          echo "Starting monitoring for error rate > ${{ env.ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD }} over ${{ env.ERROR_RATE_WINDOW }}..."

          # Poll Datadog API for error rate metric for 5-minute window, max 15 iterations (15*20s=5min)
          for i in {1..15}
          do
            # Query Datadog metrics API for error rate for financial reporting microservice
            # Replace metric_name, tags accordingly
            now=$(date +%s)
            start=$((now - 300)) # 5 minutes ago
            end=$now

            response=$(curl -s -G \
              --data-urlencode "from=$start" \
              --data-urlencode "to=$end" \
              --data-urlencode "query=avg:last_5m:financial_reporting.error_rate{env:prod}" \
              -H "DD-API-KEY: $DATADOG_API_KEY" \
              -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: $DATADOG_APP_KEY" \
              "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/query")

            error_rate=$(echo $response | jq '.series[0].pointlist[-1][1]' || echo "0")

            echo "Current error rate: $error_rate"

            # Check if error_rate is null or empty, default to 0
            if [ -z "$error_rate" ] || [ "$error_rate" == "null" ]; then
              error_rate=0
            fi

            # Compare error rate threshold
            threshold=${{ env.ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD }}
            check=$(echo "$error_rate > $threshold" | bc)

            if [ "$check" -eq 1 ]; then
              echo "Error rate exceeded threshold. Initiating rollback..."

              # Rollback deployment
              kubectl rollout undo deployment/financial-reporting

              # Notify Slack rollback triggered
              curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' --data "{\"channel\":\"${{ env.SLACK_CHANNEL }}\",\"text\":\":warning: Canary deployment rolled back due to error rate $error_rate exceeding threshold $threshold. Commit: ${{ github.sha }}\"}" $SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL

              exit 1
            fi

            echo "Error rate within acceptable limits. Checking again in 20 seconds..."
            sleep 20
          done

          echo "Canary deployment stable with error rate <= ${{ env.ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD }} over 5 minutes."

      - name: Notify Slack Canary Deployment Success
        if: success()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.23.0
        with:
          channel-id: ${{ env.SLACK_CHANNEL }}
          text: ":white_check_mark: Canary deployment successful, traffic stable. Commit: `${{ github.sha }}`"

  promote-production:
    needs: canary-deploy
    if: success()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
    steps:

  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - release/**

env:
  AWS_REGION: us-west-2
  ECR_REPOSITORY: financial-reporting-microservice
  EKS_CLUSTER_NAME: fin-prod-01
  STAGING_NAMESPACE: fin-reporting-staging
  PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE: fin-reporting-prod
  SLACK_CHANNEL: '#deployments'

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build and Push Docker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      image-tag: ${{ steps.set_image_tag.outputs.image-tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
        with:
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME }}
          role-session-name: github-actions-build

      - name: Login to Amazon ECR
        id: ecr-login
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v1

      - name: Set image tag variables
        id: set_image_tag
        run: |
          echo "GIT_SHA=$(echo $GITHUB_SHA | cut -c1-7)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          IMAGE_TAG_SHA=${GIT_SHA}
          IMAGE_TAG_LATEST=latest
          echo "::set-output name=image-tag::$IMAGE_TAG_SHA"

      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build -t $ECR_REPOSITORY:$GIT_SHA .
          docker tag $ECR_REPOSITORY:$GIT_SHA ${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:$GIT_SHA
          docker tag $ECR_REPOSITORY:$GIT_SHA ${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:latest

      - name: Push Docker image (commit SHA)
        run: |
          docker push ${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:$GIT_SHA

      - name: Push Docker image (latest)
        run: |
          docker push ${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:latest

  test:
    name: Run Unit and Integration Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          # Assuming tests are run with a script or command
          ./scripts/run_tests.sh
        # Fail early on test failure by default

  load-test:
    name: Load Testing on Staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    env:
      AWS_REGION: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      EKS_CLUSTER_NAME: ${{ env.EKS_CLUSTER_NAME }}
      STAGING_NAMESPACE: ${{ env.STAGING_NAMESPACE }}
      ECR_REPOSITORY: ${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
        with:
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME }}
          role-session-name: github-actions-load-test

      - name: Setup kubectl
        uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'

      - name: Update kubeconfig for EKS cluster
        run: |
          aws eks update-kubeconfig --region $AWS_REGION --name $EKS_CLUSTER_NAME

      - name: Deploy microservice to staging namespace
        run: |
          kubectl create namespace $STAGING_NAMESPACE || true
          helm upgrade --install fin-reporting-staging ./helm/financial-reporting \
            --namespace $STAGING_NAMESPACE \
            --set image.repository=${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${ECR_REPOSITORY} \
            --set image.tag=${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }} \
            --set replicaCount=3

      - name: Wait for deployment rollout
        run: |
          kubectl rollout status deployment/financial-reporting -n $STAGING_NAMESPACE --timeout=3m

      - name: Run k6 load test targeting staging service
        run: |
          # Install k6
          sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y gnupg software-properties-common curl
          curl -s https://dl.k6.io/key.gpg | sudo apt-key add -
          echo "deb https://dl.k6.io/deb stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/k6.list
          sudo apt update
          sudo apt install -y k6

          # Run k6 test script with environment variables
          k6 run --vus 100 --duration 10m ./load_tests/k6_load_test.js --out json=results.json

      - name: Parse k6 load test results and validate RPS threshold
        id: validate_load
        run: |
          # Extract metrics from results.json
          RPS=$(jq '.metrics.http_reqs.rate' results.json)
          ERRORS=$(jq '.metrics.http_req_failed.rate' results.json)
          echo "RPS=$RPS"
          echo "ERRORS=$ERRORS"
          # Validate RPS >= 850 and error rate acceptable (< 0.01)
          if (( $(echo "$RPS < 850" | bc -l) )); then
            echo "RPS below threshold: $RPS"
            exit 1
          fi
          if (( $(echo "$ERRORS > 0.01" | bc -l) )); then
            echo "Error rate too high: $ERRORS"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Load test passed with RPS=$RPS and error rate=$ERRORS"

  canary-deploy:
    name: Canary Deployment to Production
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: load-test
    env:
      AWS_REGION: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      EKS_CLUSTER_NAME: ${{ env.EKS_CLUSTER_NAME }}
      PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE: ${{ env.PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE }}
      ECR_REPOSITORY: ${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}
      SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
        with:
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME }}
          role-session-name: github-actions-canary-deploy

      - name: Setup kubectl
        uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'

      - name: Update kubeconfig for EKS cluster
        run: |
          aws eks update-kubeconfig --region $AWS_REGION --name $EKS_CLUSTER_NAME

      - name: Deploy canary with 5% traffic split
        run: |
          kubectl create namespace $PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE || true
          helm upgrade --install financial-reporting-prod ./helm/financial-reporting \
            --namespace $PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE \
            --set image.repository=${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${ECR_REPOSITORY} \
            --set image.tag=${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }} \
            --set canary.enabled=true \
            --set canary.trafficWeight=5

      - name: Wait for canary rollout
        run: |
          kubectl rollout status deployment/financial-reporting-canary -n $PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE --timeout=3m

      - name: Notify Slack - Canary deployment started
        uses: rtCamp/action-slack-notify@v2
        with:
          webhook_url: ${{ env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          message: |
            Canary deployment started for Financial Reporting Microservice:
            Commit SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
            Traffic split: 5%
            Cluster: $EKS_CLUSTER_NAME
            Namespace: $PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE
            Datadog Dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/financial-reporting
          status: custom
          channel: ${{ env.SLACK_CHANNEL }}

  monitor-and-rollback:
    name: Monitor Canary Deployment and Rollback on Alert
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: canary-deploy
    env:
      DATADOG_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DATADOG_API_KEY }}
      DATADOG_APP_KEY: ${{ secrets.DATADOG_APP_KEY }}
      SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
      AWS_REGION: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
      EKS_CLUSTER_NAME: ${{ env.EKS_CLUSTER_NAME }}
      PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE: ${{ env.PRODUCTION_NAMESPACE }}
      ECR_REPOSITORY: ${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
        with:
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_ROLE_TO_ASSUME }}
          role-session-name: github-actions-monitor

# CI/CD Pipeline Configuration Plan for Financial Reporting Microservice

### Target Environment:
- Kubernetes Cluster: EKS fin-prod-01
- Container Registry: Amazon ECR (us-west-2)
- CI/CD Platform: GitHub Actions
- Deployment Strategy: Canary rollout with max 5.00% initial traffic
- Monitoring: Datadog APM
- Notifications: Slack channel #deployments

## Pipeline Stages Overview

1. **Checkout & Build**
2. **Unit & Integration Tests**
3. **Build & Push Docker Image to ECR**
4. **Load Testing** (MANDATORY, enforcing CRITICAL CONSTRAINT [DEPLOY-FN82-LOAD])
5. **Canary Deployment to EKS (fin-prod-01)**
6. **Live Monitoring & Rollback on Error Threshold**
7. **Promotion to Full Production**
8. **Deployment Notification**

---

## Detailed Stage Descriptions & Configuration Notes

### 1. Checkout & Build
- Use GitHub Actions `actions/checkout@v3`.
- Build application binary and run unit/integration tests.
- Fail early on test failures.

### 2. Build & Push Docker Image
- Authenticate to AWS ECR (us-west-2) using GitHub OIDC or secrets.
- Build Docker image tagged with commit SHA.
- Push image to ECR repository corresponding to financial reporting microservice.

### 3. Load Testing (CRITICAL - DEPLOY-FN82-LOAD)
- Execute load tests simulating realistic traffic.
- Use a load testing tool such as k6 or JMeter configured to test sustained throughput.
- Define threshold: sustain >= 850 requests per second (RPS).
- Fail pipeline if threshold not met.
- Note: This stage blocks promotion to production if load test fails.

### 4. Canary Deployment Rollout
- Deploy new version to EKS fin-prod-01 using a canary deployment strategy.
- Initial traffic split: 5.00% routed to new version, 95.00% to stable version.
- Use Kubernetes deployment tooling (e.g., Argo Rollouts, Flagger) or custom scripts to control rollout.
- Ensure canary rollout is gradual and traffic split is configurable but capped at 5%.

### 5. Monitoring & Automatic Rollback
- Integrate Datadog APM to monitor error rates and performance metrics in real-time.
- Configure alerts or checks on error rate metric:
  - Rollback trigger condition: error rate exceeds 2% over any rolling 5-minute window.
- Rollback mechanism should automatically revert to the previous stable version upon trigger.
- Implement health checks and readiness probes to avoid traffic to unhealthy pods.

### 6. Promotion to Full Production
- Upon successful canary period with no rollback trigger:
  - Shift 100% traffic to new version.
  - Confirm stability via Datadog monitoring.

### 7. Deployment Notification
- Notify Slack channel `#deployments` at key points:
  - Deployment started
  - Canary deployment successful
  - Rollback triggered (if any)
  - Full production promotion
- Use GitHub Actions Slack integration or webhook with appropriate message formatting.
